newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Hydro outlines investment, gearing.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Hydro outlines investment, gearing.

text.p: Electricity generator Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc said on Thursday that its plans to buy out United Utilities, its 50-percent joint venture partner in Keadby power station, would raise net gearing to around 50 percent.
The company said pre-tax profits for the six months ending September 30 dipped to 61.3 million pounds from 61.7 million pounds a year ago and it paid out a dividend of 5.28 pence, up from 4.75 pence.

Scottish Hydro said it expected to complete the takeover of Keadby by the end of the financial year and added that, with existing expenditure commitments, gearing should peak at around 65 percent in 1998/99.

The company said that action in hand to raise output and reduce costs would further improve performance over the next two to three years, and raising service standards "even further" was a key aim, with more progress expected.
It said turnover had grown by 7.4 percent despite competitive and regulatory pressures.
"The second half of the financial year has started well and we are confident of an encouraging result for the full 12-month period," it added.
